item.title: Adventure World: Pandas, Safari and Marine Shows in Shirahama — Guide
item.description: Adventure World, just outside Shirahama, is Wakayama’s biggest family attraction, combining a zoo, a safari park and a marine park on one large site. Its greatest fame comes from its giant pandas: the park has run one of the world’s most successful panda breeding programmes outside China, and is one of only a couple of places in Japan where visitors can see them. Beyond the pandas, a safari zone can be toured by bus, tram or on foot past lions, rhinos and giraffes, while the marine section stages dolphin and orca performances, making for a full and varied family day.

item.title: Oji Zoo: Kobe's Family Zoo Under the Cherry Trees — Guide
item.description: Oji Zoo is Kobe’s much-loved city zoo, a compact and refreshingly inexpensive place set in parkland between Nada and Sannomiya. Its collection covers the usual favourites — elephants, big cats, giraffes and a well-known group of koalas — alongside a small old-fashioned amusement corner with rides for younger children and a preserved Meiji-era Western residence in the grounds. In spring the zoo’s cherry trees make it one of the best hanami spots in central Kobe, when families picnic under the blossoms between animal enclosures.

item.title: Wakayama Family Trip: Pandas, Beach Fun & Kid-Friendly Temples
item.description: Wakayama works well for families in a way that some of Japan’s more densely cultural prefectures do not: there are genuine natural spectacles that children find compelling without requiring adult interpretive scaffolding, a world-class animal park that delivers on its panda promise, beaches that are genuinely safe for small children, and a spiritual mountain that manages to be simultaneously solemn and otherworldly enough to captivate curious kids. The distances between main attractions require planning — this is not a prefecture you can improvise with young children — but a well-structured 3–4 day itinerary produces one of the most varied family travel experiences in western Japan.
